properties.bedrock_lithology: Carboniferous sandstone (Craigleith and Hailes strata) interbedded with siltstone and basalt intrusions
properties.stratigraphy: Glacial till mantle over dense sedimentary sandstone bedrock
properties.drainage: Well-drained sloping topography toward the Water of Leith valley
properties.local_lithics: Craigleith blonde sandstone ashlar, Scottish slate roofing tiles

properties.primary_surfacing: Fine-grained macadam roadway with dressed granite kerbstones and sandstone flagstone pavements
properties.micro_grading: Gentle northwest downward slope toward Water of Leith
properties.wear_patina: Historic urban weathering with subtle mineral leaching along flagstone joints

properties.understory: Pruned domestic hedging and ivy clinging to boundary retaining walls

properties.typology: Victorian / Late Georgian residential terraced townhouses (Edinburgh New Town West End)

structures.roof_geometry: Mansard and pitched slate roofs with prominent dressed stone chimney stacks and party parapet walls
structures.facade_material: Finely dressed blonde Craigleith sandstone ashlar with channelled rustication at ground level and canted bay window projections
structures.weathering_patina: Historic atmospheric soot toning with crisp dressed stone stringcourses and stone balustrades

structures.roof_geometry: Hipped slate roof with lead capping and dormer projections
structures.facade_material: Rusticated sandstone basement/ground with ashlar upper storeys
